subject: A0576BEEDEFBE1D30BDBD486E037E8EB
introduction: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá returned to the apostles whenever he wanted to show what faith does with ordinary material: fishermen and a tax-gatherer, “neither name nor trace”, mocked while they lived, who after their Master’s death recovered from grief, scattered across the world and outlasted the empire that killed them. He told it to small Bahá’í groups who felt their own insignificance. The New Testament tells it with more shadow, and the passages set here keep both: “unlearned and ignorant men”, “the offscouring of all things”, “earthen vessels”; and also Peter’s tears and the day the women’s news seemed “idle tales”.
questions: What, according to the readings, turned fishermen into apostles?
Why does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stress their lack of learning? Is he against learning?
The Gospels record the apostles’ failures. Does that strengthen or weaken the example?
Who are the overlooked people in whom the readings would have us expect something?

outside.why: The apostles were just as other men are. They perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, and they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
Few in number, with no helper. Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
Outwardly fishermen and dyers. God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty.
Peter and John, once simple workmen. Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

They had neither name nor fame; now they are known everywhere. The Preacher thought no one was remembered: there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever. What accounts for the exception?
People mocked them. We are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day.
The weakest souls, made strong by the Holy Spirit. We have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.
Lacking in culture, but alive; Herod was learned and dead. Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
From this focus the bounty was reflected on the disciples. Ye are the light of the world.
Peter, Andrew, John and Mary Magdalene attained. Thou art the Christ. Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee.
A question about the resurrection. The two at Emmaus: did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?

Peter was a fisherman and became the great apostle. He was also the one who denied, and went out, and wept bitterly. The readings mention the denial rarely. What does it add to the picture of an “ordinary life”?
After the crucifixion the disciples wept and thought the Cause lost. The women’s report seemed to them as idle tales.
On that day they received a new spirit. They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues.
And the charge under which they scattered across the world: go ye therefore, and teach all nations.

shortfall: The fifty readings make one point many times, that obscure men changed the world; companions were set where the telling adds something.
